title: The Central Tower
subtitle: A silent and merciless order of ideals.

trails.title: Prison Reform Notes
trails.description: Look, the smallest of clues, the greatest of structures, built brick by brick.

content.text:
During the third Comala Congress, ███'s daily dose of diazepam was reduced from two and three-quarter tablets to none, replaced with two classified poetry collections (A1675) and sixty chlorpromazine tablets, to be taken one and a half per day.

1. Two days, eleven hours, eight minutes, and four seconds later, an eight-millimeter crack appeared on a bar of his cell, which is on the second floor, near the third staircase, and is the eighth cell from the left. He scraped off a four-by-three-millimeter fragment from the thirty-second tile.

2. Mentions of "the other me" increased from three times in 48 hours to twenty-five times in 48 hours.

3. Four days, three hours, seven minutes, and eight seconds later, he transitioned from merely collecting manuscript paper to collecting manuscript paper and mirror fragments. Within the next twenty-four hours, he collected eleven mirrors, which totaled one hundred and three shards.

...

During the sixth Comala Congress, ████'s supply of fluoxetine and valproate was completely discontinued, replaced with four classified L6759 literary selections and four rolls of 400 cm bandages.

1. ... Averaged thirty-two bangs against bars and walls per hour. The bandages were all used up within four days, fourteen hours, twenty minutes, and nine seconds, with 89.3 cm lost in the water due to excessive ripping.

2. ... Wrote fifteen pages of poetry over ten days, six hours, eight minutes, and three seconds. Tore up fourteen of those pages and swallowed the remaining one.

...

trails.title: On Zeno Defectors
trails.description: I wonder if the tower inside the prison has seen this.

content.text:
...

Based on the above information and recent intelligence from the Timekeeper's squad, it is confirmed that Zeno's defector unit had entered Comala Prison, which held numerous arcanists, and withdrew from Ushuaia on March 2nd. The operation clearly involved cooperation with Manus Vindictae. The current whereabouts of the defectors remains unclear, pending further intelligence from the Timekeeper's squad.

*The information is fragmented and primarily inferential. For the full reasoning behind the operation and additional details, please refer to Attachments 4-28.

items.text: The Central Tower

items.speaker: García
items.text: Easy, easy! It's me, García! We met at the gallery earlier.

items.speaker: García
items.text: Please. I come in peace.
Recoleta pays no mind to the young man's explanations; her focus holds on the woman beside him.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It's you, Octavia! The murderer herself!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, calm yourself, Ms. Recoleta.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The jailer has already confirmed that she wasn't the one to fire at the Idealist. The shot came from somewhere else in the room.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Hmph.
Recoleta bites her lip, giving up a little space to the intruders.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Octavia, what brings you here at this hour?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: I come here out of goodwill. Believe me, I didn't want any bloodshed either.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: I understand you just arrived today. There's something you need to know about the inmates here.
Their visitor's expression is weary and low.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: We're outcasts rejected by society and literature, and our privileges are limited within these walls. But before I started my own literature group, I struck a deal with the Panopticon authorities.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: If we cooperate and stay out of trouble, they'd leave us be. We could discuss literature freely and openly in Comala. Such a thing may seem trivial to you, but this is of immense importance to us.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Oh, there's no happier thing in this world than discussing literature! No one should ever put limits on it!

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: You're right, Recoleta. But we're prisoners here. There are certain rules we have to follow.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Except, the Idealist didn't see it our way. He refused to compromise, believing that the long poem and his so-called "-ism" could break us free from the cage of the ever-watchful eye.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Perhaps he was right. You might've achieved more if you'd listened to him. After all, visceral realism keeps us connected to who we are.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You have to believe in the truth of visceral realism! Because out there, beyond these walls, many of us still do!

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: And what has it changed? García, you're the latest inmate here. Tell us, three months ago, before they arrested you and took you here ...

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: What has the visceral realism movement accomplished out there?
Beside them, García, who had been patiently leaning against the railing, produces a metallic vibration on its grates. A rough paper roll burns between his lips.

items.speaker: García
items.text: At first, it was revolutionary. Young poets joined in droves. We held gatherings, and the literary world seemed alive again.

items.speaker: García
items.text: I was just a kid when the leading poets left the city. Everyone thought it was only temporary. But they didn't come back, and nothing has happened since.

items.speaker: García
items.text: No one says it, but we all know: visceral realism died in 1977.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: No. Not for me.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It's not dead as long as people still believe in it. I believe in it!
Octavia ignores the childish remark. She knows that "conviction" can be as fragile as a spider's web.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Belief, faith—what is this obsession with the "true self"?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Why does your type always insist on there being a true self hiding beneath our roles in society, our disciplines?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Look at the Idealist! He never once stopped fighting for what he believed in, even long after he was put behind these bars.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: "Idealist," what a name he gave himself. Who will he be when he finally breaks free from the eyes of the central tower? When he's left without his willful audience? A nobody, that's what.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: And that is a truth even he is terrified of.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Octavia. I hope you've come with something more important to share than just some criticism of the Idealist.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: You're right. I have an important message for you.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Dr. Dores—I heard you were looking for her. The woman from the São Paulo Veterans' Residence. She used to write under the name "Urd," didn't she?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, that's right. Do you know her? You're the first person I've met here to speak plainly about her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you know where she might be?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: We crossed paths, but only briefly. I'm not sure where she's gone. Maybe the authorities know.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: However, she left this with me. I think you'll need it more than I do.
Octavia hands over her personal folder.
Before they might open it, she has already turned to leave.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: We have other matters to attend to. I'll leave you to your business. García, shall we?
Their visitors leave in haste, their faces and expressions obscured by the night's shadows.
The Foundation's investigators open the worn manuscript folder with caution.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "The Physician told me the horrifying truth about the Panopticon of Comala and the power behind it—Manus Vindictae."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "By becoming the Panopticon's sole patron, they seized control of the resources and the allocation system, turning this place into a living hell. I suspect that the Physician, the current highest authority here, is responsible for this situation."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "... I discovered that the inmates were put through brutal training, even when they were too sick to carry out their tasks. They also forced pure-blood arcanist inmates to wear their masks, effectively turning them into murmuring puppets ..."

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Just as we suspected, Manus Vindictae is orchestrating everything.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: No wonder we didn't find them in the city. They've been hiding here all along.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No one would've thought to come looking for them here.
They snap the folder shut.
A familiar signature, seen on the foreword page of UTTU magazine, and the receipt found in São Paulo's Heartfelt Home.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But why would Ms. Octavia bring this to us? What's in it for her?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Do you think she's trying to mislead us, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Maybe. But the handwriting in that notebook is most certainly Urd's.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If she's leading us astray on purpose, why? Ms. Recoleta, what do you think? Could she be Aleph?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Not a chance! Haven't you seen how she denies everything beautiful in the world? Aleph would never be so biased.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: No, Aleph is like a mirror. He reflects both light and shadow.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: But Octavia ... Maybe she hasn't looked at the shadow within for a long time.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I know that look on her face. It's the look of a writer.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I've seen so many like her during my trip—the faces of a lost, struggling generation.
Under the night sky, Comala Prison stands like a forgotten gravestone covered by fine, cold snow.
In a room repurposed from a prison cell, three girls in search of someone share an absurd, bizarre tale. Meanwhile, at the entrance of the central watchtower, a jaguar knocks on a secure door.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: *deep breath* Dr. Merlin, I'm here to report on today's events.
Come in.
Central Tower Waiting Area
Frantic writing breaks the quiet of the room.
The jailer's visit does not deter the man behind the desk. He continues writing, wholly absorbed, as if each letter were filling the world around him.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: There was a commotion in the gallery today, sir.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: An inmate known as the Idealist was severely injured. The inmates nearby said he lost consciousness from blood loss.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: However, after we put everyone back in their cell, the Idealist was gone. I made a sweep of the grounds, but there was no trace of him.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: It's possible that he regained consciousness and went into hiding. I'll perform a full search tomorrow.
The jaguar finds herself quite unexpectedly concealing the truth about Pablo.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: No need.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Sir?

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: He knew the consequences of breaking the rules, did he not?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Sir, with all due respect, I think today's incident proved just how dangerous it is to let the inmates keep their weapons.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: We never should've let them walk around with deadly weapons! Even if we had to, we should've doubled the guards. We can't expect them to follow their own rules simply out of fear of the central tower.
The Physician interrupts her sharply, with no hint of concern.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: Such matters fall beyond your purview, Jailer. You only need to do what's required of your title.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: Is there anything else?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: There is another thing. Two guests from the Foundation came through today. They said they were looking for someone named Dores.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: They've shown a willingness to cooperate. Though, they were involved with the incident in Corridor Zero.
The sound of writing continues. Her report is disregarded. The jailer takes a deep breath. The next part is difficult to say.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Sir, there is one more thing.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I told Ms. Octavia we're short on rations, and she's adjusted the inmates' portions accordingly. But that won't last long.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Manus Vindictae stopped providing supplies back in March, and Zeno has collected all the prisoners they had previously placed in our custody.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I just wonder why they have so suddenly withdrawn from Ushuaia and brought all their prisoners with them.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I also noticed that we haven't received any orders from the government since Warden Tartuffe was transferred.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: In fact, we haven't had any communication with them at all.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Sir, in frank terms, we're facing down a serious shortage of medicine, food, and basic supplies. At this rate, the Panopticon will soon be unable to operate. Where will our inmates go then?
The man before her says nothing for a long time, his pen still flickering over the page.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Can we ask the Foundation for help? Th-They've sent their people here. Maybe they're interested in the Panopticon?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I could arrange a meeting if you like.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: You're unusually talkative today.
The man finally stops writing and looks up.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Pardon, sir?

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: It's fascinating, you know. You've become so much more concerned about this place and its inmates than when you first started. You are now dictated by your title.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I didn't mean to overstep. I'm sorry.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: You can go now. I have a great deal of work to do. Oh, and one more thing.
He beckons the jailer back before she leaves.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: Make sure this month's Comala Congress is held according to schedule.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Yes, sir.
The jaguar disappears beyond the door, metallic footsteps fading into the distance. Only then does the Physician allow his suppressed frustration to surface.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: How many times have I warned you about this? The Idealist has to go. He's nothing but trouble for us! You're too soft on him, Aleph. Look at the mess he has us in now!

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Calm down.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: He's a rabble-rousing thief, a self-destructive maniac, a snake in the grass.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: He even stole the Tear of Comala from me. He's nearly ruined everything we've worked for!
The man angrily raises the once-lost and now-found die.
In the dim room, it flickers with a comforting glow.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: It's only a die, Merlin. It does nothing more than a die can do.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: You were there today. You saw what he did. He managed to change the Panopticon with this die, even if only for a second.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: He'll ruin my work, Aleph. He's a slave to his passion; his head is filled with impulsive thoughts. I don't trust him. We can't trust him!

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: I've done everything you've asked. Now it's time to do your part.
Aleph responds with indifference to the Physician's frustration, continuing his writing without pause.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: Time's ticking down. I can't afford any further mistakes. No one can be permitted to stop my experiment in the Panopticon.

items.speaker: The Physician
items.text: I'll prove it to them that we've found the path to the ultimate answer.
